question: Can a preference agent gain reliable extra weak supervision when some fitting examples share an alternative?
feasibility: Use only the fitting side of the primary training payload. Construct a directed graph of observed wins from exact strings. Discard self-pairs and conflicting direct observations. For each observed pair test if its direct outcome is predictable by an unambiguous two-edge path through a third distinct alternative without using that direct edge. Count each unordered pair once, whichever way it appears. Report aggregate agreement and the number of independent connected components involved.
gate: Before generating any weak labels require at least 30 such checked directed relations across 10 connected components, and a Wilson 95 percent lower bound above 0.55, plus at least max(20, 1 percent of fitting rows) new unordered pairs with one direction of two-hop support and no direct observation. Pairs with opposite evidence or a previously conflicting observation cannot be added. This rule screens the viability of an experiment; the bound describes pairs and does not assume that pairs inside a component are independent for final inference.
if_viable: Carry the same graph builder into the fit worker and recompute all evidence inside every training fold. Train one consenting pair-encoder head on the measured data plus these weak pairs with individual weight at most 0.25 and at most 10 percent total original weight. Fit vocabulary, scaling and all encoder transformations on real fitting rows only. The highest supported actual compatible trial by primary feedback nominates the template. Compare the new head and its equal vote with the established two-model reference across three disjoint training folds. Require a strictly positive gain on all three and >=0.003 pooled gain on the first two before any fresh autonomous raw run. Register actual fits and cause of early stop.
data: No validation/test input or answer, no H2, no paid API. No weak label is described as an observed click result. The released default and its PR remain available throughout.
